b.answer:
Worked example: a junk filter on Harvest Lane's HL · Form order → Sheet Zap.

Step 2 · Filter by Zapier, renamed "Drop tests". Rule: Name (from step 1) · (Text) Does not contain · test. Say it as a sentence: "Only continue if the name does not contain test."

Capitalisation. Test with both "Test order" and "TEST TEST". If either slips through on your account, add Formatter · Text · Lowercase on the name before the filter and check that output instead.

Four entries:

EntryNameExpectedZap history
1Mrs AdebayocontinuesSuccess · 1 task (sheet row)
2Tunde BakarecontinuesSuccess · 1 task
3Test orderstopsFiltered · 0 tasks
4TEST TESTstopsFiltered · 0 tasks

Open a Filtered run: the filter step shows which condition failed, and the sheet step never ran. Tasks used: 2, not 4.

Watch out: "Testimony Adeyemi" also contains "test". If you have customers with that name, check a prefix instead (Name starts with "test") or add a hidden "is_test" field to your test form.
mistakes: Using "Contains test" instead of "Does not contain", so only test entries continue.
Placing the filter after the sheet step, so test rows are saved and tasks are used anyway.
Not thinking about real names such as Testimony that contain the word.
b.pass: Zap history shows two successful runs and two Filtered runs for the four entries, and the Filtered runs used no tasks.
b.redo: Send it back if a test entry reached the sheet, the filter sits after a task-using step, or capitalised "TEST" wasn't tried.

s.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane's order router, built on the 1.2 Zap.

Added steps: 2 · Filter "Drop tests" (Name does not contain test). After the fee lookup, a second Lookup Table "Zone": Bodija, Mokola, Ring Road, Challenge → inside; fallback → outside. After Format Currency, Paths:

BranchRulesSteps
A · Prioritytotal (step 6, number) Greater than 50000Orders row · PRIORITY email · Filter zone = outside · Logistics row
B · Outside zonetotal Less than 50001 AND zone Exactly matches outsideOrders row · Logistics row
C · StandardfallbackOrders row · normal email

Truth-table test results:

#OrderTotalZoneExpectedZap history
12 crates, Bodija26500insideCC ran · A, B skipped
2Small order, Oyo town13500outsideBB ran · Logistics row added
3Hotel order, Bodija92000insideAA ran · inner filter stopped Logistics
4Hotel order, Oyo town92000outsideA onlyA ran · Logistics row added · B skipped
5Name "Test Tunde"——FilteredFiltered at step 2

Check the outputs: Orders has 4 new rows (one each, no duplicates); Logistics has 2 (orders 2 and 4); Tolu received one PRIORITY email for each of orders 3 and 4 and one normal email for order 1.

Submit: five Zap history screenshots (no keys or customer phones visible), each labelled with its branch, plus the truth table.
mistakes: Branch B without "total Less than 50001", so order 4 runs A and B and creates two Orders rows.
Path rules compare the Format Currency text instead of the step 6 number, so A never runs.
Checking the raw Area instead of the zone from the lookup, so "Bodija " goes outside.
Testing only the happy path and skipping the big out-of-zone order.
s.pass: Five labelled Zap history screenshots in which every order takes exactly the branch in the truth table, order 4 creates one Orders row and one Logistics row, and the test order shows Filtered.
s.redo: Send it back if any order runs two branches or none, a screenshot is missing, or keys or customer details are visible.

g.answer:
Worked example: a clearly fictional school in Abeokuta, "Brightway College", routing admission enquiries from its website form (fields: parent name, phone, level, boarding).

Rules said as sentences: secondary boarders go to the boarding housemaster; secondary day pupils go to secondary admissions; nursery and primary go to the primary office (no boarding below secondary); anything else goes to the bursar's assistant to call back.

Truth table, written before building:

LevelBoardingBranch
nurseryno / yesC · Primary office (boarding note added)
primaryno / yesC · Primary office (boarding note added)
secondaryyesA · Boarding
secondarynoB · Secondary day
missing or otheranyD · Fallback: call back

Paths: A = level Exactly matches secondary AND boarding Exactly matches yes. B = level Exactly matches secondary AND boarding Exactly matches no. C = level (Text) Is in nursery, primary. D = fallback. A Formatter Lowercase and Trim on level and boarding come first.

Results:

TestExpectedRanOK
nursery, noCCyes
primary, yesCCyes
secondary, yesAAyes
secondary, noBByes
"JSS 2", blankDDyes
live: "SS1", yes (day 3)DDcaught by fallback

Submit: the truth table, a screenshot of the four branches' rules, a Zap history screenshot per test row, and one line on the fallback catch ("Parents write JSS/SS, so I added those to the level dropdown").
mistakes: Fewer than four real outcomes, for example two branches plus a fallback.
Building first and writing the truth table afterwards to match what was built.
No "missing data" row, so the fallback is never tested.
Overlapping rules (e.g. "boarding is yes" alone) that send a secondary boarder down two branches.
g.pass: A truth table covering every combination plus a missing-data row, one Zap history result per row with exactly one branch each, and evidence that the fallback caught at least one case.
g.redo: Send it back if any row is untested, any row ran two branches, or the fallback has never run.
